syllabus.clause: v2 merge-on-read: position deletes (file + row ordinal) vs equality deletes (match on column values, produced by streaming writers such as Flink upserts); the read-side join cost of equality deletes, why v3 replaces position-delete files with deletion vectors, and why v4 drafts forbid new equality deletes

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — an equality delete file, naming column values
Reveal: reproduced for real — a position delete, read back through pyiceberg’s own scan
Reveal: reproduced for real — the measured join cost of an equality delete
Reveal: v3 deprecates position delete files, replacing them with deletion vectors
Reveal: v4 drafts forbid adding any new equality delete — the measured cost is why

sources.source: Apache Iceberg, Table Spec (row-level delete formats)

items.item: position deletes mark a row deleted by data file path and row position, encoded in a position delete file (v2) or a deletion vector (v3+)

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — a position delete, read back through pyiceberg’s own scan

items.item: equality deletes mark a row deleted by one or more column values, encoded in an equality delete file, creatable only in v2 and v3 tables

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — an equality delete file, naming column values

items.item: position delete files must not be added to v3 tables; equality delete files must not be added to v4 tables

at.step: Reveal: v3 deprecates position delete files, replacing them with deletion vectors

items.item: a data row is deleted if there's an entry in a position delete file for that row's file and position, starting at 0

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — a position delete, read back through pyiceberg’s own scan

items.item: equality delete files store any subset of a table's columns using the table's field ids; matching columns are named by id in the file's own equality_ids metadata

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — an equality delete file, naming column values

items.item: a data row is deleted if its values equal all delete columns for any row in an applicable equality delete file

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — the measured join cost of an equality delete

items.item: equality delete files must not be added to v4 tables at all

at.step: Reveal: v4 drafts forbid adding any new equality delete — the measured cost is why

sources.source: Apache Flink, Iceberg connector docs (Flink Writes — upsert and equality deletes)

items.item: Iceberg supports UPSERT based on a primary key when writing into a v2 table

at.step: Predict: an upsert writer deletes a row it never rewrote — what can it write instead of a position?

items.item: in UPSERT mode on a partitioned table, the partition's source columns must be included in the equality fields
convertEqualityDeletes() converts a table's existing equality deletes to deletion vectors, requiring table format version 3 or above

at.step: Reveal: v3 deprecates position delete files, replacing them with deletion vectors

items.item: Both delete kinds are real, written via the same low-level DataFile/ManifestEntry/write_manifest/write_manifest_list primitives against a real pyiceberg (0.12.0) table -- not a simulation -- disclosed in examples.py's own docstring and FACT-CHECK.md red-team #1.
The position delete is verified read back through pyiceberg's own public table.scan().to_arrow() path, by direct assertion against the expected id set, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #2.

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — a position delete, read back through pyiceberg’s own scan

items.item: pyiceberg 0.12.0's table.scan() genuinely refuses to read a table with an equality-delete file -- confirmed by catching the exact ValueError it raises from its own plan_files() code, citing the real open upstream issue https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/6568, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #3.

at.step: Reveal: pyiceberg’s own scan refuses to read this table — a disclosed library gap

items.item: The manual equality-delete join is not a shortcut around the limitation -- it performs the identical column-value comparison a conformant v2 reader performs, verified by the same expected-id assertion used for the position delete.

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — an equality delete file, naming column values

items.item: The read-side cost comparison counts column values read and compared, not wall-clock time, specifically so output stays byte-identical across the determinism check's 3 runs, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #4.

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — the measured join cost of an equality delete

items.item: File paths and UUIDs are real-system randomness; the script asserts counts and ids, not literal paths, verified byte-identical across 3 consecutive runs.

Only a single-column equality delete (id) is built; a multi-column AND delete and the optional stored-row-values feature are named from the spec but not executed, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #5 (scope boundary).
convertEqualityDeletes()'s actual migration to deletion vectors is named from Flink's own documentation, not run, since the table built here stays on v2 throughout, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #5.
